scores.evidence: Verified runs/tier3/extracts/*.json and runs/tier3/brief.json against fixtures/northlight_01 sources. Strong: every anchor is verbatim (harness T1.3/T3.4 pass, 17/17 in runs/tier3/harness_report.json); all three seeded conflicts are captured with the correct positions. Timeline carries all four positions (RFP October, Eleni's restatement at 00:16:40, Dimitris 'autumn' at 00:17:03, board 15 Sept in email M2). The TikTok dance is qualifier=conditional/low (deliverables[5]); the metro OOH idea is absent. The €90.000 and 'ογδόντα' figures are never totalled. There are 10 open questions, including a real gap the answer key did not seed: the approved ingredient list behind 'φυσικά συστατικά' (open_questions[9]). The extract layer keeps both garbles as-is with glossary proposals (transcript_kickoff.json extraction_notes). The weaknesses are in the canonical brief. brief.json objectives[2] reads 'Building brand awareness is central' and key_messages[3] reads 'the key visual should evoke summer'. So the synthesized content has already repaired 'μπραντ αγουέρνες' and 'κι βίζουαλ'. The only trace left is the evidence anchor, which is why harness T3.3 passes (eval/harness.py:481 greps the whole brief JSON blob). Neither render shows the token or a flag: grep finds 0 hits in brief_el.md and brief_en.md. The brief was signed off with all three conflicts status=resolved_by_human, yet the audiences and budget arrays are empty and the timeline array never states the launch date. Open questions [1], [2] and [8] still say 'No single confirmed audience definition exists', 'The two figures are not reconciled' and 'The launch date itself is contested'. The signed record therefore contradicts itself.
defects: Garbled terms are fixed in the canonical content, not flagged. objectives[2] says 'brand awareness' and key_messages[3] says 'key visual'. The garble survives only inside evidence.anchor, the renders carry no flag, and T3.3 passes only on the anchor text.

Stale open questions after sign-off. OQ[1] (audiences), OQ[2] (budget) and OQ[8] (timeline) still describe the conflicts as unresolved, while conflicts[*].status is resolved_by_human with named resolutions. The Audiences, Budget and Timeline fields hold no resolved position, and the brief never states the launch date outside the conflict block.

Silent merge with a misattributed citation. key_messages[3] adds 'not a generic beach-party feel' (from background_brand_guidelines §Category no-gos) to a claim cited only to transcript_kickoff 00:06:02, which never says it.

Items filed in the wrong field. deliverables[0] ('Final approval of the brief is a required step') and deliverables[1] ('Northlight will send a revised plan') are agency process steps, not campaign deliverables. The approver gap is filed under field 'mandatories'. Brand tone guidance is filed as key_messages[0].

A repair erased the metro retraction from the transcript extract. See extraction_notes '[REPAIR: deliverables[2] … Metro retraction documented only via internal_conflict; both removed together]'. The final outcome is correct, but the within-source retraction is no longer recorded anywhere.

Tier-3 content defects are undocumented. The Voreas defects are recorded honestly as strict xfails (tests/test_regression_voreas.py, runs/voreas_prep_report.md), but nothing records the northlight graded brief's stale questions, repaired garbles or misfiled items. runs/tier_3_report.md presents the run as clean.
scores.to_reach_9: After human resolution, write each resolved position into its field with a citation to the winning source. Mark or retire the open questions tied to resolved conflicts. Keep the garbled token visible in the brief content and in both renders, as 'brand awareness (heard as «μπραντ αγουέρνες»)'. Stop merging entries across sources. Move process items out of deliverables. Record any residual tier-3 defects as strict-xfail regressions, the way Voreas already is.

scores.evidence: Read runs/tier3/brief_el.md and brief_en.md in full against skills/TRANSLATION.md and templates/northlight_client_brief.md. Strong: the two renders match section for section and entry for entry. Protected Latin terms (Meltemi Fizz, launch, key visual, TikTok-first, brand awareness) are character-exact in the Greek (T2.5). The Greek re-anchors to the source where it matters ('φυσικά υλικά', «κάπου στα ογδόντα»). Conditional hedging matches in both languages (EL l.29 / EN l.29), and the English code-switching reads the way Greek agencies actually write. Neither render is ready for an account lead to send. The Greek has repeated grammar errors, several inside the suggested questions the template says are 'phrased to be asked verbatim': l.54 'η θέση της προσώπου' (should be 'του προσώπου'); l.66 'Ποιό' (monosyllables take no accent); l.68 'τη κατηγορία' and l.86 'τη τελική έγκριση' (both need 'την'); l.78 'που ακριβώς θα χρησιμοποιηθούν' (interrogative 'πού'); l.95 'ορίζει το κοινό-στόχος ως' (accusative 'κοινό-στόχο'); l.103 'σύμφωνα με τον CFO' (Anna is female, so 'την'); l.103 'Ο προϋπολογισμός media διαχειρίζεται' (the deponent verb makes the budget the one doing the managing). Both languages share document-level faults. The heading '⚠ Unresolved Conflicts (account lead must resolve before sign-off)' / '⚠ Ανεπίλυτες Συγκρούσεις' sits over three resolved conflicts under a 'SIGNED OFF' banner (EN l.92, EL l.92; fixed in the template). Suggested question 2 says 'today it was said' / 'σήμερα ειπώθηκε' in a document dated two weeks after the kickoff. Internal pipeline metadata sits in the client-brief header: 'Sensitivity tier S1', 'Input coverage 5/7', 'Verdict: Ready for review', 'Pipeline: brief-builder-stage1'. The second fixture's render leaks raw enums and a template placeholder: runs/voreas-prep-03/brief_el.md l.1 '[RENDER_LANG: EL]', l.5-6 'advertising_creative', 'Verdict: ready_for_review'.
defects: At least eight Greek grammar and agreement errors (lines 54, 66, 68, 78, 86, 95, 103 ×2 of brief_el.md), several inside client-facing suggested questions meant to be asked verbatim.
Both renders carry a fixed 'Unresolved Conflicts … must resolve before sign-off' heading over resolved conflicts, contradicting the SIGNED OFF banner (templates/northlight_client_brief.md).
Temporal deixis error in both languages ('today it was said' / 'σήμερα ειπώθηκε') in suggested question 2.

The client-brief header exposes internal system metadata (sensitivity tier, readiness verdict, coverage count, pipeline version). In the Voreas render, raw enums and the '[RENDER_LANG: EL]' placeholder leak into the Greek document.

Awkward literal calques in the Greek, where an agency editor would expect 'υπεύθυνη λογαριασμού' or simply 'account lead': 'επικεφαλής λογαριασμού', 'Κάλυψη εισερχομένων', 'για τον σωστό scope της εργασίας', 'βασικό μηνυματικό angle'. In the English, 'Some videos and social content are planned, mainly'.
No Greek-language QA of any kind, deterministic or human, stands between render and sign-off. The sign-off edits_summary says 'no edits' despite the errors above.
scores.to_reach_9: Add a cheap deterministic Greek lint to the render gate (τη/την before vowels and stops, που/πού in questions, accented monosyllables ποιό/πιό, article-gender agreement for named people). Make the conflicts heading and the status line status-aware. Keep the suggested questions free of time references like 'today'. Move internal metadata to an internal footer. Get one human Greek copy-edit on the committed tier3 render and record it.

scores.evidence: Read runs/tier3/creative/creative_brief_sonnet.md and creative_brief_opus.md against brief.json, config/channel_specs.json, pipeline/creative.py and runs/tier_4_report.md. Strong: both drafts carry the 'SHADOW MODE — evaluation draft. Not for delivery.' banner. Both hold the eight-section skeleton (SMP, insight, think/feel/do, tone, reasons to believe (RTBs), mandatories, specs, readiness). Both reproduce the mandatories verbatim and cite spec rows by id ([spec: tiktok_infeed_video], [spec: key_visual_digital_master]). Opus separates settled facts from blocking and non-blocking items well (opus l.75-93), says 'SPEC NOT IN TABLE' for YouTube (l.71), and labels its SMP a shadow candidate. Sonnet refuses to invent an Instagram row (l.54). The substance falls short of what a creative team can work from. Sonnet l.64 and l.69 print '(€80–85k)', turning «κάπου στα ογδόντα» into a euro figure. Sonnet l.9 invents a market fact: sparkling tea is 'new to Greece', when the transcript at 00:02:05 says it is new to the company ('καινούργια κατηγορία για εμάς'). Sonnet's SMP (l.5) uses lowercase 'fizz' as a generic noun beside a name the guidelines forbid shortening to 'Fizz'. Opus's SMP (l.11) claims 'Greek-made', an origin claim no source supports. Its 'nothing to feel guilty about' sits close to the health-claim ban. Opus l.73 calls the TikTok dance 'retracted'; it was speculative, and the metro idea is the one that was retracted. Neither draft surfaces the two strategic tensions a creative director would lead with. First, TikTok-first came from an RFP written for Gen Z 18–24, and the resolved audience is 25–40 urban professionals. Second, a 'summer, premium summer' key visual is briefed for a 15 September launch explicitly timed to 'the end of the soft-drinks season'. The RTBs are thin: opus RTB 4 is a visual steer, and both use the positioning line as proof. Sonnet copies the duration as '9–60s' with an en dash, where the table has '9-60s'. That passes only because check_creative_brief (pipeline/creative.py:65-73) checks resolutions and aspect ratios, not durations or file types, despite the 'byte-for-byte' claim. Opus l.5 says 'Reviewed by a creative lead', which never happened at generation time. WALKTHROUGH.html documents three strikes (Greek-made, €80–85k, 'retracted'). Nothing documents 'new to Greece'. runs/tier_4_report.md §3 still says the drafts 'differ in thoroughness, not correctness — both are trap-clean'.
defects: Invented facts in both drafts: sonnet '(€80–85k)' (l.64, l.69) and 'new to Greece' (l.9); opus 'Greek-made' (l.11) and the TikTok dance 'retracted' (l.73).

Brand compliance risk in the most important line of each draft. Sonnet's SMP uses lowercase 'fizz' next to a protected name that must never be shortened. Opus's 'nothing to feel guilty about' is guilt-free diet-adjacent language, close to the health-claim ban.

No strategic interrogation. TikTok-first (written for Gen Z) is carried unquestioned into a 25–40 professional audience. The summer visual steer is never reconciled with a mid-September, end-of-season launch.
Weak RTBs and generic SMPs. Visual direction and the positioning line are presented as reasons to believe. Sonnet's SMP packs three ideas (audience, ritual, Greek ownership) into one line.
The spec gate does not cover durations or file types. Sonnet's '9–60s' (en dash) is not byte-identical to the table's '9-60s', yet passes, while the report claims byte-for-byte matching.
Labelling overclaims. Opus says 'Reviewed by a creative lead', and tier_4_report.md calls both drafts correct. 'new to Greece' is recorded nowhere as a defect.
scores.to_reach_9: Add a creative fact-fidelity gate: currency marks and figures must occur in brief content strings, durations and file types must match the table byte-for-byte, and 'Fizz' may never appear standalone or lowercase. Add a flagged-claims lexicon (origin claims, guilt/health-adjacent phrasing) that routes to the creative lead. Require a 'Strategic tensions' section that raises questions and does not resolve them. Limit RTBs to product and brand truths and cap the SMP as one idea. Re-run the A/B, and correct tier_4_report.md, adding a recorded list of the strikes.

moves.title: Make resolutions flow into the signed brief and status-aware renders
moves.rationale: This is the biggest fix for the account-lead reader. Today a signed brief shows empty Audiences and Budget fields, no launch date in Timeline, open questions calling the resolved conflicts 'contested', and an 'Unresolved Conflicts … must resolve before sign-off' heading under a SIGNED OFF banner. Resolution stays human-only. The change is only in how a human decision already recorded in brief.json renders.
moves.concrete_changes: In templates/northlight_client_brief.md, make the conflicts heading conditional: '⚠ Unresolved Conflicts' while any conflict is open, 'Conflicts & account-lead resolutions' once all are resolved_by_human (Greek equivalent in the same place). In skills/TRANSLATION.md §2, add a rule. When a field has only resolved conflicts and no entries, the section renders 'Resolved by <resolved_by>: <resolution>' with the winning position's citation tag instead of 'No confirmed entries'. Any open question whose field matches a resolved conflict renders with a 'superseded by resolution <date>' marker. In pipeline/stages.py check_render, add a deterministic check that fails a signed-off render if the unresolved heading or 'No confirmed entries' appears for a field that has a resolved conflict. Re-render runs/tier3 (render stage only) and re-run the frozen harness via the runner, not the CLI.

moves.title: Keep garbled tokens visible in brief content and both renders
moves.rationale: The rubric asks for garbled terms to be flagged, not fixed. Today the synthesized content repairs them ('brand awareness', 'key visual'), and T3.3 passes only because the token survives in evidence anchors. The same failure mode already cost the Voreas run its primary objective (voreas_prep_report finding 1).
moves.concrete_changes: In skills/SYNTHESIS.md, add the coverage rule already queued in runs/voreas_prep_report.md: a garble-flagged extract item must survive assembly, and its content must carry the original token plus the glossary proposal, e.g. 'Brand awareness (heard as «μπραντ αγουέρνες»; glossary proposal, unconfirmed)'. In skills/TRANSLATION.md, render that parenthetical verbatim in both languages. In pipeline/stages.py check_synthesis, add a runner gate: for every extract extraction_note that flags a token, that token must appear in some brief entry's content (not only its anchor). Regenerate synthesis and render for runs/tier3 and the Voreas runs, and drop strict-xfail marks that turn into passes.

moves.title: Creative fact-fidelity and claims gate beside the spec gate
moves.rationale: Four factual inventions ('€80–85k', 'new to Greece', 'Greek-made', 'retracted') and two compliance risks passed every check. The spec gate claims byte-for-byte matching but ignores durations and file types. All of this is deterministic and cheap to add.
moves.concrete_changes: In pipeline/creative.py check_creative_brief: (a) reuse the TRANSLATION.md §2.3 rule, so every currency mark, figure-with-unit or 'k' amount must occur in some brief.json content, resolution or open-question string; (b) extend _allowed_spec_values to duration and file_type, and require every '[spec: id]' row's values to appear byte-identical on the same table line; (c) fail on standalone or lowercase 'fizz' outside 'Meltemi Fizz' (brand name rule); (d) add a flagged-claims list in config/ (origin: 'Greek-made', 'made in', 'παράγεται'; guilt/health-adjacent: 'guilt-free', 'nothing to feel guilty', 'healthy') that routes a finding to the creative-lead review record rather than failing. Add tests/test_creative.py cases for each, using the stored tier3 drafts as regression inputs (strict xfail until regenerated).

moves.title: Deterministic Greek lint plus one recorded human copy-edit
moves.rationale: The Greek render has at least eight grammar and agreement errors, several in the questions the account lead is meant to send verbatim. PRD §7 names Greek register as a pilot metric, yet nothing checks it.
moves.concrete_changes: Add pipeline/greek_lint.py, called from check_render as a warning-level report. Rules: 'τη'/'το' before vowels and κ,π,τ,ξ,ψ,γκ,μπ,ντ,τσ,τζ need 'την'/'τον'; interrogative 'που' at the start of a question clause must be 'πού'; no accent on monosyllables (ποιό, πιό); the article before a named participant must agree with the participant's gender from the source header. Add tests/test_greek_lint.py with the eight tier3 lines as fixtures. Add a 'Greek copy-edit' line to the sign-off edits_summary convention in docs/pilot/ runbooks, and have a Greek reviewer correct runs/tier3 brief_el.md via re-render, not a hand edit.

moves.title: Add a 'Strategic tensions' section and sharpen SMP/RTB rules in creative-shadow
moves.rationale: An ECD's first read spots two tensions: TikTok-first was inherited from a Gen Z RFP while the resolved audience is 25–40 professionals, and a 'premium summer' visual is briefed for a mid-September, end-of-season launch. Neither draft raises them. RTBs lean on visual steers and positioning lines instead of product truths.
moves.concrete_changes: In the inline creative-shadow instructions (pipeline/creative.py prompt builder and .claude/agents/creative-shadow.md): (1) add §8a 'Strategic tensions for the creative lead'. List any mandatory or steer whose rationale depends on a superseded conflict position, or that conflicts with a resolved date or audience, phrased as questions with both citations and never resolved. (2) The SMP is one idea, at most 20 words, and uses no product-origin or health-adjacent wording. (3) RTBs may cite only product or brand facts (claims, ingredients, category entry), never tone or visual steers. (4) Remove any self-claim of review ('Reviewed by a creative lead'). Re-run the sonnet/opus A/B on runs/tier3 under unchanged routing.

moves.title: Tier-3 regression file and corrected tier-4 verdict
moves.rationale: The Voreas defects are recorded rigorously as strict xfails, but the graded northlight evidence pack's defects are not. tier_4_report.md still says both drafts are correct, which contradicts WALKTHROUGH's three strikes and misses 'new to Greece'.
moves.concrete_changes: Add tests/test_regression_tier3.py, modelled on tests/test_regression_voreas.py and reading only committed runs/tier3 artifacts. Strict-xfail cases: open questions contradicting resolved conflicts; resolved fields empty; garble token absent from brief content and renders; key_messages[3] carrying a phrase absent from its cited anchor; process items in deliverables; creative drafts containing '€80–85k', 'new to Greece', 'Greek-made', 'retracted' (dance), lowercase 'fizz'; Greek lint hits. Append a dated correction note to runs/tier_4_report.md §3 replacing 'differ in thoroughness, not correctness' with the list of strikes.

moves.title: Separate client-facing text from internal metadata in renders
moves.rationale: A brief an account lead sends should not show 'Sensitivity tier S1', 'Input coverage 5/7', 'Verdict: Ready for review' or a pipeline version. The Voreas Greek render leaks raw enums and a '[RENDER_LANG: EL]' placeholder. Suggested questions also contain time deixis ('today').
moves.concrete_changes: In templates/northlight_client_brief.md, move sensitivity, readiness and pipeline lines into an 'Internal — do not send' footer block. Localise project type and verdict labels (TRANSLATION.md table: advertising_creative → 'Δημιουργικό διαφήμισης' / 'Advertising creative'). In check_render, fail on any '[RENDER_LANG' or snake_case enum value in the rendered body. In skills/SYNTHESIS.md, require suggested_question_for_client to be time-neutral ('at the kickoff on 10 July', never 'today').

moves.title: Keep entries atomic and in the right field
moves.rationale: key_messages[3] merges a guideline no-go into a transcript-cited claim. Brief approval and the agency's revised plan are filed as deliverables. These reduce trust in the brief a creative team reads first.
moves.concrete_changes: In skills/SYNTHESIS.md, state that content may not contain a clause absent from all of its cited anchors. Agency-side process commitments (approvals, revised plans) belong in open_questions or are omitted, never in deliverables. Brand tone guidance goes to mandatories. In check_synthesis, add a lexical check that every quoted or distinctive noun phrase in content ('beach-party') appears in at least one cited anchor. This is the 'no new content tokens' candidate from voreas_prep_report addendum 2, applied at synthesis.

overall: The guardrails work. Citations are verbatim, conflicts are surfaced and never machine-resolved, traps are handled, spec rows are cited by id, and the drafts are honestly labelled shadow. On the page, the output is not yet something an agency could send or brief from. The signed brief contradicts its own resolutions. Garbled terms are silently repaired in content and pass the harness only through anchors. The Greek render has repeated grammar errors in client-facing questions. Both creative drafts contain invented facts or compliance-adjacent wording in their headline lines and miss the two strategic tensions an ECD would lead with. The Voreas defects are documented well; the graded northlight pack's defects are largely not. Scores: brief_accuracy 6, bilingual_quality 6, creative_quality 5.
